messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: error-rate spike detected on serving-runtime (eu-west-1). Autoscaler note: 12% 5xxs over 2m. Primary error: 'CUDA illegal memory access' from model-host pool. Runbook 3 triggered.
oncall-ruby: I'm on it. Picking up triage. Which machines?
Alice Eng: logs point to nodes gpu-13,gpu-14 in pool model-host-a. Seeing repeated:
```
[2026-03-17T12:01:02Z] CUDAError: illegal memory access at 0x7ffdeadbeef
backtrace: runtime::dispatch -> kernel_launch -> gpu_mem_map
```
Ben SRE: Ty. I'm checking node health and dmesg. Running `kubectl get pods -n serving -o wide | grep model-host-a`
Ops Bot: Action: cordon node gpu-13 -> `kubectl cordon gpu-13` (initiated).
Maya CS: Any customer impact? we've got an open ticket from AcmeCorp complaining about 502s. Need ETA for customers.
oncall-ruby: Initial impact estimate: 1.8% of requests in eu-west-1 failing with 5xx during the spike window. Routing fallback already triggered for some routes to cpu-fallback model.
Alice Eng: Repro steps from logs: reproducer job OOMs within 60s when sequence lengths > 4096 and KV cache hits high. Hypothesis: kernel race when map/unmap of pinned buffers during concurrent eviction.
Ben SRE: dmesg shows repeats: `NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: GPU fault: 13 00 0000` and kernel reports `invalid device address`. I'm grabbing perf and nvcrash dumps.
Alice Eng: Quick mitigation: scale down parallelism for that pool and enable software fallback for long contexts. Rolling a config patch to serving-config on model-host-a: set MAX_CONCURRENCY=8 and ENABLE_PREFIX_CACHE=false.
Ops Bot: Patch rollout started -> canary on model-host-a/gpu-14 (1 pod). Health checks passing so far.
Maya CS: I'll draft a customer notice: brief, mention we're mitigating and affecting <2% of requests, EU region, recommending retry/backoff.
oncall-ruby: If canary stays green 3m, we roll to remainder and cordon/drain gpu-13 for deeper kernel inspection. Ben, please prepare node reboot plan and kernel logs export.
Ben SRE: On it. Will upload nvcrash + dmesg to the incident artifact bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/7001002345/ and open a hardware ticket if needed.
Alice Eng: Also enabling model fallback chain: if cuda illegal access observed -> switch to quantized-compat variant on different pool. Patching runtime policy: `fallback.model_priority = [quantized-compat, cpu]`.
oncall-ruby: Ops Bot reports canary trending: error-rate down 80% on canary. Rolling to remaining 5 pods.
incident-bot: Update: runbook step 7 completed (canary rollback policy applied). Incident severity: P1. Postmortem owner assigned: Alice Eng.
Maya CS: Customer update drafted, pinging legal for wording. I'll post to status.redwood.ai once we have stable rollback.
Ben SRE: draining gpu-13 now (`kubectl drain gpu-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`) then will repro in isolated host image.
Alice Eng: Note for postmortem: collect kernel traces, nv_driver version, model version, sequence-length distribution, and KV cache hit rates. Suspect race on buffer unmap under eviction.
oncall-ruby: Thanks team. Keep updates here every 10m. If any node shows ECC errors, escalate to hw team immediately.
Ops Bot: Log snapshot uploaded: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/7001002345/logs.tar.gz
incident-bot: If customer impact rises >5% escalate to Incident Commander.
Ben SRE: Reboot complete on gpu-13, nvcrash dump attached. No ECC errors, but driver RX logs show `unmapped address` spikes at the same timestamps as crashes.
Alice Eng: I'm attaching a quick patch to the runtime that adds an atomic fence around buffer unmap; will test on canary after confirming logs.
Maya CS: Sent initial customer notice to impacted accounts (AcmeCorp + 3 others). They acknowledged, want timeline.
oncall-ruby: Tentative ETA for full remediation: 45-90 minutes depending on repro. Postmortem to follow.
Ben SRE: Leaving note: nodes gpu-13/gpu-14 taken out of rotation. Creating tracking ticket: INC-7001002345.
Alice Eng: Thanks all — ping me @here for any urgent regressions.
incident-bot: End of thread snapshot at 7001002600.
